title: Camellia Altitude
description: A singing octave line moves above fine left-hand arpeggios. Its phrases lengthen into five, then contract into a three-beat exchange of bass octaves and upper thirds. The opening returns with altered bass colours before settling on a clear A-major sixth.
difficulty: Advanced cantabile octaves, supple position changes and mixed metre
technical_note: Voice the upper edge of the RH octaves, releasing and relocating the hand between attacks without losing the sung line. The LH sixteenths require an even thumb passage under that broad phrase. In the three-beat section the octaves pass to LH beneath moving RH thirds.

performance.note: The upper octaves sing over light sixteenths. Give the LH octave answer the same warmth, then release the growing phrase into A major.

composition_time_source: Recorded when the first score was saved.

audio_reverb.description: Subtle warm room; preserve the clarity of moving voices.
